figures.caption: Figure 2: Overall illustration of BEST. The framework consists of four core modules: (1) Hierarchical Transformer Encoder (Stage 1): it employs frequency-channel attention and iTransformer layers to encode neural activity into phoneme/character representations with hierarchical temporal masking; (2) Phoneme-Character Fusion Block (Stage 1): a lightweight convolutional fusion module aggregates hierarchical neural representation to bridge neural and linguistic spaces; (3) Lightweight Speech Translator (Stage 2): a lightweight speech translator generates autoregressive text sequences from fused embeddings; and (4) KenLM Reranking (Stage 2): a custom 4-gram language model resolves ambiguities from noisy neural signals for final selection.

Table 1: We compare the speech-BCI framework on the Brain-to-Text ’24 and ’25 hold-out set. Gray background indicates the pipeline without the language model. Some results lack detailed data as the corresponding code is unavailable; see the competition leaderboard for more details. ⋆, ⋄, • denote the most lightweight network, the most robust network, and the most practical network, respectively.
Table 2: Performance comparison across different decoders with parameter counts and finetuning strategies on T15. Gray background indicates the audio-based LLM decoders.

Figure 4: Cross-day generalization under temporal shift. Models are trained on first 15 days (left) and 18 days (right), and evaluated on subsequent days.
